content.user_title: Compose Type-Safe Go Workflows with samber/mo
content.value_statement: Optional values and repeated error checks can make multi-step Go workflows difficult to maintain. This skill guides explicit type choices and composable samber/mo pipelines.
actual_capabilities: Explain when to use Option, Result, Either, or plain Go values.
Guide Option integration with JSON serialization and nullable SQL columns.
Show conversion between Go tuples, pointers, and samber/mo types.
Compose type-changing transformations with sub-package Map, FlatMap, and Pipe functions.
Explain mo.Do, safe value extraction, and error propagation.
Describe Future, IO, Task, and State with focused usage examples.
limitations: Requires a Go project and a compatible samber/mo version for executable examples.
Provides guidance and examples, not an independent runtime, compiler, or test runner.
Does not replace native Go error handling or nil-safety guidance outside samber/mo.
Examples need compilation and behavioral tests, especially for JSON omission and map lookup conversion.

use_cases.title: Model Nullable API Fields
use_cases.description: Choose Option fields for nullable SQL columns and JSON responses, with explicit null and omission behavior.

use_cases.title: Simplify Internal Error Pipelines
use_cases.description: Compose configuration loading, parsing, and validation with Result while preserving conventional public API signatures.

use_cases.title: Explore Deferred Computations
use_cases.description: Compare eager Future computations with lazy Task and IO abstractions before choosing an execution model.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Core Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether [field or operation] needs Option, Result, Either, or plain Go. Compare absence, failure, and valid alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Model Nullable Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt [Go struct] to samber/mo Option fields for nullable SQL values. Explain JSON null versus omission and the required Go version.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a Result Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [read, parse, validate workflow] using samber/mo Result sub-package functions. Preserve errors and return a conventional tuple at the public boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Design Deferred Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [deferred workflow] with samber/mo Task or IO. Explain Future timing, error handling, and tests for execution order and failure propagation.

output_examples.input: Should a cached user and a fresh user use Result?
output_examples.output: Use Either when both outcomes are valid alternatives. Handle each variant explicitly; use Result when one outcome represents failure.

output_examples.input: Why can my Option integer not become a string through its direct Map method?
output_examples.output: Direct Map preserves the type parameter. Use option.Map from the sub-package for a type-changing transformation, then compose further steps with Pipe functions.

output_examples.input: Should an absent Option field disappear from JSON automatically?
output_examples.output: None normally serializes as null. For field omission, verify Go 1.24 or later and use the omitzero tag with compatible Option behavior.

best_practices: Choose types from domain meaning: Option for absence, Result for failure, and Either for valid alternatives.
Use sub-package functions when types change, and preserve conventional tuples at public Go API boundaries.
Compile examples and test absent values, errors, JSON output, and panic-sensitive extraction.
anti_patterns: Wrapping every value in Option when ordinary zero values already express the domain.
Using direct Map or FlatMap methods for transformations that change generic type parameters.
Calling MustGet on uncertain values outside a deliberate panic-handling boundary.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and references for selecting and composing samber/mo types in Go projects.

faq.question: Does the skill install samber/mo automatically?
faq.answer: No bundled installer is provided. The documentation shows a go get command that changes project dependencies when executed.

faq.question: When should I keep plain Go error handling?
faq.answer: Keep plain Go for simple operations, conventional public interfaces, or workflows requiring explicit error inspection at each step.

faq.question: Can direct Map methods change the wrapped type?
faq.answer: No. Use the relevant sub-package functions for transformations between different wrapped types.

faq.question: Does Option automatically omit absent JSON fields?
faq.answer: None normally becomes null. Omission requires appropriate serialization settings, such as omitzero on Go 1.24 or later.

faq.question: Does Task start its computation immediately?
faq.answer: Task defers computation until Run is called. Future starts asynchronously on construction, so choose based on execution timing.
